claims.limitations: Finite reproduction using one numerical backend. It is far below the published record and cannot establish the universal statement RH.
claims.statement: FLINT/Arb isolated 10,000 ordered critical-line Hardy-Z roots, and Turing counts account for every nontrivial zeta zero below the final separator T approximately 9878.2187131956.

claims.limitations: Lagarias's theorem quantifies over every positive integer. A positive finite prefix cannot prove RH.
claims.statement: The Lagarias inequality is certified for every integer 1 <= n <= 1,000,000, with equality only at n=1.

claims.limitations: One positive finite compression cannot prove RH or exclude negative directions elsewhere. The negative omission control is deliberately corrupted and has no implication for RH.
claims.statement: The complete finite Weil matrix A=P-R-S for c=5/2 and modes -4 through 4 is positive definite by nine interval LDL^T pivots; deleting its sole p^r=2 term produces a certified negative mutation control.

claims.limitations: This certifies one finite 256-to-512 contraction using one FLINT/Arb backend. It gives no N=512 lower bound and does not establish the uniform k>=9 recurrence required for the Nyman limit and RH.
claims.statement: A direct exact-dyadic primal witness and a fresh replay of the certified N=256 lower endpoint prove d_512^2 < (449/500)d_256^2, so the normalized optimal block gain is greater than 51/500.

claims.limitations: This rejects one explicit eight-dimensional trial space at the single 256-to-512 extension using one FLINT/Arb backend. It does not reject other trial spaces, establish the uniform k>=9 recurrence, or prove or disprove RH.
claims.statement: For the frozen eight-column arithmetic trial space at the N=256 to N=512 extension, fixed-order interval LDL^T proves F_V > (9/10)U_256 and therefore its optimal captured gain Gamma(V) is strictly less than d_256^2/10.

claims.limitations: This exact finite audit does not prove the log(2) integral identity or the infinite divergence theorem, which remain an external human-auditable bridge in the cited 2005 preprint. The theorem rejects only the first one-coefficient-at-a-time Vasyunin correction, not all Vasyunin or Nyman constructions, and does not prove or disprove RH.

scope.arithmetic: exact integers and reduced rational multipliers

claims.statement: For every 1 <= n <= 4096, the first Vasyunin greedy recurrence matches the two-adic Mobius closed formula, preserves exact interval interpolation, and has the recorded exact rational L1 and squared-L2 increment multipliers; at all twelve nontrivial powers of two those multipliers are 1/2 and n/4.

claims.limitations: This exact finite audit checks one frozen two-point shell only through X=4096. The all-shell non-little-o theorem is an external human-auditable analytic bridge, not a finite extrapolation. The result does not cover scale-dependent regularizations and does not prove or disprove RH.
claims.statement: For the frozen shell y_9=1, y_16=-1, every finite Mobius extension, divisor inversion, direct/factored slope, and integer-interval alias identity agrees exactly through X=4096.

claims.limitations: This certifies one complete finite-dimensional contraction for one explicit exact-dyadic vector. It gives no uniform all-scale estimate and does not prove or disprove RH.
claims.statement: For one explicit exact-dyadic N=256 old Nyman vector and one explicit balanced K=16 correction supported through index 8192, the complete infinite weighted-L2 direct gain is greater than 7/50000.

claims.limitations: This proves a general finite-support periodic-tail lemma and one complete finite-dimensional contraction. It gives no uniform all-scale energy-to-gain estimate and does not prove or disprove RH.
claims.statement: If an old vector and a finite balanced correction are both supported through Q, their periodic direct-gain partial sums are bounded by Q(Q-1)(rho+tau); for the frozen N=256, K=16 direction this proves complete infinite weighted-L2 direct gain greater than 1/5000 using a prefix through 2^22.

claims.limitations: This certifies six independently selected finite contractions, not a nested recurrence. It proves no arbitrary-N continuation or uniform energy-to-gain estimate and does not prove or disprove RH.

scope.uniform_finite_gain_lower_bound: gain>1/(20N) for the six declared N values

claims.statement: For each N in {8,16,32,64,128,256}, one explicit exact-dyadic balanced K=64 correction has positive complete infinite weighted-L2 direct gain under T=32768N; all six declared rows satisfy gain greater than 1/(20N).

claims.limitations: This certifies one linked chain of length two. The companion frozen-prefix theorem proves that an indefinitely append-only harmonic-balanced continuation cannot drive the energy to zero. The finite gains neither prove nor disprove RH.
claims.statement: For explicit exact-dyadic vectors p1=p0+a1 and p2=p1+a2, where the verifier reconstructs p1 before deriving a2, the two complete infinite weighted-L2 direct gains are greater than 1/150 and 1/9000, and their telescoped sum is greater than 61/9000.

claims.limitations: The proof is human-auditable rather than formally checked. It rejects only corrections that remain outside a fixed finite seed core and have zero harmonic sum; overlapping, rebased, or harmonic-changing constructions remain open. It does not prove or disprove RH.

scope.correction_condition: support strictly above the initial finite core and sum(a_n/n)=0
scope.theorem_inputs: elementary interval identities, Mobius inversion, and Bertrand's postulate

claims.statement: Every append-only harmonic-balanced correction chain from every finite Nyman seed freezes a nonzero initial residual interval and therefore has a fixed positive weighted-L2 norm floor; this architecture cannot drive the Nyman distance to zero.

claims.limitations: The proof is human-auditable rather than formally checked and rejects only a fixed nonzero finite source with its natural hard cutoff. It does not reject scale-dependent shells, balanced finite multipliers, or genuinely multiscale constructions, and does not prove or disprove RH.
claims.statement: For every nonzero finitely supported real y, S(X)=sum_{n<=X}(mu*y)(n)/n is not o(X^(-1/2)); consequently the natural sharp alias sections do not converge to f_y in L2((0,infinity),dt/t^2).

claims.limitations: No finite set of positive compressions controls every Fourier mode and a cofinal unbounded family of cutoffs; the universal positivity theorem remains missing.
claims.statement: Finite-prime Weil quadratic forms are the primary candidate-witness and proof-bridge research track.
